transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because I'm having a real hard time keeping my focus on the job. I'm a construction manager, and... well, I can start out a safety briefing or sit down to review some plans, really trying hard to pay attention. But within just a few minutes, my mind is already off thinking about three other problems on the site. Because of that, I end up missing things—important things I know I should have caught. It's getting pretty bad, and I need to figure out what's going on.
When did you first start noticing these concentration problems? Have you always had trouble focusing, even back in school, or is this something new that's developed more recently?

It's definitely not new. It goes way back. I mean, even back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents about it. They'd say I couldn't stay in my seat, or that I talked out of turn. I was always losing my homework, too. And... well, I'd just rush right through the directions on assignments before I really understood what I was even supposed to do. So, yeah, it's been happening since I was a kid.

You mentioned these focus problems have been going on since childhood. But I'm wondering—has anything changed recently? Are your concentration difficulties worse now than they were, say, a year or two ago, or have they pretty much stayed about the same level?

Well, I guess the underlying issue has always been there, but... yeah, it has definitely gotten worse recently. I'd say it's been seriously disrupting my job for about two years and two months now. That's right around the time the construction schedule changed at work. The hours got a lot more chaotic, and ever since then, it's just been a real struggle to keep up and keep my head straight.

Over these past two years when things got worse, have you been feeling persistently sad or down, or have you been experiencing a lot of worry and anxiety? Or has it mainly just been the focus and attention problem without those mood changes?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I mess up at work, but I'm not depressed or anything. And I don't really sit around worrying or feeling anxious, either. It's really just the focus... the fact that my brain won't stay on track when I need it to. That's the main thing.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) - patient denies persistent worry and anxiety. Ruled out F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder) - patient denies persistent sadness or depressed mood.
